description: Periodically executes SELECT queries against tables and views in a SQL Server database and emits the resulting rows as documents.

spec.sslPolicy: TDS encryption is forced on unconditionally: the DSN is built with 'encrypt=true' AND 'TrustServerCertificate=true' hardcoded, so the channel is encrypted but the server certificate is never verified. There is no user-facing TLS/SSL config field and no way to supply a CA or turn verification on.
spec.tunnelSupport: Optional SSH bastion tunnel via the shared networkTunnel package (networkTunnel.sshForwarding.{sshEndpoint,privateKey}). When in use the tunnel forwards the configured host:port to localhost:1433 and a custom mssqldb HostDialer redirects the TCP dial there while still advertising the real hostname as TLS SNI / TDS LOGIN7 ServerName.

defaultSchedule.description: advanced.poll, defaulting to the Go duration string '24h' when unset. Grammar accepts either a Go duration ('5m', '6h', '1h30m') or the literal form 'daily at HH:MMZ' (UTC only), enforced by the JSON-schema pattern ^([-+]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?(h|m|s|ms))+|daily at [0-9][0-9]?:[0-9]{2}Z)$. No cron syntax is supported.

continuity.notes: Pure client-side polling: the connector creates no server-side objects at all (no replication slot, no change table, no scratch table, no consumer group) - it only issues SELECTs. All resumption state (per-binding CursorNames, CursorValues, LastPolled, DocumentCount) lives in the Flow checkpoint, so pausing between polls costs nothing on either side and resumption is unbounded in time. The real cost of a missed tick is fidelity rather than continuity: a cursor-incremental binding only ever sees rows whose cursor columns advance, so DELETEs and in-place updates that do not bump the cursor are invisible regardless of poll frequency, and intermediate states between two polls are collapsed. Deletion inference exists only for keyless full-refresh bindings (collection keyed on /_meta/row_id), where a shorter result set than the previous poll emits synthetic op:'d' tombstones for the trailing row IDs. Concurrency is capped at maxConcurrentQueries = 1 across all bindings, so many bindings sharing one schedule serialize. A watchdog Fatal-kills the task after 6h with no first row, or 15m of silence mid-result.

any TABLE_TYPE other than 'BASE TABLE' or 'VIEW' (same Go-side rejection path)

schedule.description: Go duration string or 'daily at HH:MMZ'. Each binding runs its own worker goroutine but all bindings share a global semaphore of weight 1, so only one query executes at a time.

cursorColumns: <user-supplied resource.cursor columns; discovery does NOT recommend any>
backfill.chunking: Not chunked. The initial poll issues ONE unbounded query for the entire table (no LIMIT/TOP, no OFFSET/FETCH) and streams the result set. Boundedness comes from streaming + checkpointing, not from the SQL: a checkpoint is emitted once at least 1000 documents have accumulated AND the cursor tuple is about to change value, persisting the PREVIOUS row's cursor so no row sharing a cursor value can be skipped on resume. A mid-query restart therefore re-runs from the last persisted cursor rather than resuming inside the result set.

incremental.chunking: KEYSET (seek) predicate, not OFFSET/FETCH — there is no OFFSET, FETCH NEXT, TOP or row-number windowing anywhere in the connector. The cursor tuple from the last row of the previous poll is bound as positional parameters @p1..@pN and the whole remaining tail is streamed in one query. Strictly greater-than semantics mean rows that tie the persisted cursor on a later poll are never re-read, so a non-unique cursor column can drop rows written after the poll that observed that value.

streams.name: <schema>/<table> — full-refresh table with a primary key

schedule.description: Go duration string or 'daily at HH:MMZ'.

snapshot.chunking: None. With resource.cursor empty the template drops both the WHERE and the ORDER BY, and every poll re-reads the whole table in a single query. Checkpoints are emitted every 1000 documents with no cursor-boundary constraint. Because the collection is keyed on the source primary key, re-reads reduce to upserts; rows deleted at the source are never removed.

schedule.description: Go duration string or 'daily at HH:MMZ'.

snapshot.chunking: None; whole table per poll. When the source table has no primary key the collection falls back to the key /_meta/row_id and rows are numbered 0..N-1 in result order. Documents get /_meta/op = 'c' or 'u' by comparing the new row id against the previous poll's document count, and if a refresh returns FEWER rows than the last one, synthetic op:'d' tombstone documents are emitted for the surplus trailing row ids. Row identity is positional, so any reordering of the unordered result set rewrites unrelated rows.

schedule.description: Go duration string or 'daily at HH:MMZ'.

snapshot.querySketch: Arbitrary user-supplied Go text/template rendered with { IsFirstQuery: bool, CursorFields: [already-bracket-quoted cursor column names], SchemaName, TableName } and the helper funcs add/quoteTableName/quoteIdentifier. The rendered string is executed verbatim with the persisted cursor values bound positionally as @p1..@pN. This bypasses the built-in template entirely, so chunking, ordering and cursor-safety are whatever the user writes. Only 'name' is required on such a binding; schema/table may be omitted (in which case SourcedSchema emission is skipped for it).

authTierRationale: The only credential mode is a plain SQL Server DSN assembled from address/user/password/database (default user 'flow_capture'), with no OAuth, no app registration, and no token exchange anywhere in the connector. The optional SSH tunnel adds a second self-serve secret (a private key the customer already owns) but does not change the tier. Nothing is issued or brokered by a hosted control plane.

unionMisfits.description: The schedule grammar is neither 'interval' nor 'cron'. schedule.Parse accepts exactly two forms: a Go duration string (time.ParseDuration, so '5m', '6h', '1h30m', and per the JSON-schema pattern also 'ms' and signed values) or the literal prefix 'daily at ' followed by an HH:MMZ time-of-day in UTC only. The duration form is a plain sleep-after-last-poll delay (periodicSchedule.Next = after + period), NOT an aligned wall-clock interval, so the effective period drifts by the query duration on every tick. I used kind 'other' for both, but a consumer that maps 'other' to a fixed interval will get the daily form wrong and one that ignores the drift will mis-predict tick times.

PullSpec.chunking assumes a bounded slice per request. This connector has no such concept: one poll = one unbounded SELECT over the entire remaining tail, streamed row-by-row, with resumability provided by checkpoint emission rather than by SQL. The bound between polls (the keyset predicate) and the bound within a poll (checkpoint cadence at cursor-value boundaries) are two different mechanisms, and only the former is expressible here.

A single binding's disposition is decided at RUNTIME by the shape of the Flow collection key, not by the connector config: the poll loop tests whether the collection key is exactly ['/_meta/row_id'] and only then synthesizes /_meta/op values and trailing deletion tombstones. The same table config yields 'merge' or 'snapshot_with_tombstone' depending on a downstream property, which the schema models as a static per-stream field.

cursorField is a single nullable string, but the cursor here is an ORDERED TUPLE of columns (resource.cursor is a []string, and the template emits an N-term lexicographic predicate). It is also never recommended by discovery — discovered resource configs ship with no cursor at all, so the user must choose the columns. I put the tuple in pull.*.cursorColumns and left cursorField null.

The exclusion list is not unconditional: the four schema-name exclusions (INFORMATION_SCHEMA, PERFORMANCE_SCHEMA, SYS, CDC) are emitted ONLY in the else-branch when discover_schemas is empty. Supplying an allowlist that names one of them would capture from it. The excludes field has no place to record that conditionality, so I encoded it in the strings.

abstained.streams[].name: This is a discovered-schema connector: there is no literal stream list anywhere in the code. Every entry above is an ARCHETYPE (kind: 'archetype') describing one capture shape the code can produce; actual names are derived at connect time as recommendedCatalogName(schema, table) = '<lowercased-sanitized schema>/<lowercased-sanitized table>' with the resource name being '<table>' for the 'dbo' schema and '<schema>_<table>' otherwise.
abstained.streams[].cursorField: Left null on every archetype. The cursor is an ordered tuple (resource.cursor, a []string), not a single field, and crucially discovery never populates it — generateSQLServerResource emits only {Name, SchemaName, TableName}, so a freshly discovered binding is full-refresh until a human adds cursor columns. Naming any specific column here would be a guess.
abstained.streams[].primaryKey (archetypes 0 and 1: The concrete key columns come from the customer's INFORMATION_SCHEMA.KEY_COLUMN_USAGE at discovery time and cannot be known statically. Only the fallback for keyless tables (/_meta/row_id) is fixed in code.
abstained.streams[3].primaryKey: A template-override binding may produce arbitrary result columns; the collection key is whatever the user configures downstream, and the connector performs no key inference for it.
abstained.streams[].supportedSyncModes (archetype: A custom template can implement either shape depending on whether it references .IsFirstQuery / .CursorFields; the connector cannot tell which, and neither can I.
abstained.execution.continuity.resumeWindow: Not applicable rather than unknown — no server-side retention window exists to expire, since the connector reads only base tables and stores all resume state in the Flow checkpoint.
abstained.paginator: No HTTP transport, so no paginator exists anywhere in this connector.
